title: Should the Window named properties object return supported named properties in [[OwnPropertyKeys]]?
body:
Given `data:text/html,<iframe name=123>` with `Reflect.ownKeys(window.__proto__.__proto__)`…

* Gecko returns ["123", Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag)]
* Blink returns [Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag)]
* WebKit returns [Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag)]

This seems to be why Firefox fails the [[OwnPropertyKeys]] subtest of [/webidl/ecmascript-binding/window-named-properties-object.html](https://wpt.live/webidl/ecmascript-binding/window-named-properties-object.html), but I can’t figure out what the correct behaviour is according to the spec. This is how far I got:

* [WindowProxy](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#windowproxy) (the wrapper with indexed access) has [an exotic [[OwnPropertyKeys]]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#windowproxy-ownpropertykeys)
* [“This document does not define a complete property enumeration order for platform objects implementing interfaces (or for platform objects representing exceptions). However, it does for legacy platform objects by defining the [[OwnPropertyKeys]] internal method as follows.”](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-ownpropertykeys)
    * so legacy platform objects have an exotic [[OwnPropertyKeys]] that includes supported property names (subject to [named property visibility](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-named-property-visibility)), but for other platform objects the behaviour of [[OwnPropertyKeys]] is undefined?
* [Window](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#window) itself (the interface with named access) is [Global], so Window objects are [not legacy platform objects](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-legacy-platform-object)

Have I missed something? Does this mean both Gecko and Blink and WebKit are correct?

(cc @domenic, on behalf of servo/servo#29396)
